chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by Ka'b ibn 'Ujra, and lice were scattering from his head while he was in Ihram. So he (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do the insects of your head harm you?' He said: 'Yes.'
So whoever among you is sick or has an ailment of the head, he (should effect) a compensation by Fasting or alms or sacrificing.

So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered him to shave his head, and made the fasting to be for three days, and the charity to be upon six poor ones, for each poor one being two Mudds, and the sacrifice a sheep.
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'And everything in the Quran where it says

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a person in Ihram who suffers from head lice?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the legal principle of 'al-khayr' (choice) in Quranic exegesis, specifically regarding the fidya for breaking Ihram due to head lice or illness. It establishes that when the Quran presents options using the conjunction 'or' without specifying a hierarchy, the individual retains the discretion to select any of the prescribed compensations—fasting, feeding the poor, or sacrificing a sheep. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence for handling ritual impediments, linking the specific incident of Ka'b ibn 'Ujra to the broader theological understanding of divine ease in worship.
